Definition: of Hebrew origin (H54); Abiathar, an Israelite:--Abiathar.
BiblicalUsage: Abiathar appears once in the New Testament, in Mark 2:26, when Jesus defends His disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath: 'how he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread.' Jesus reaches back to David's flight to make His point about mercy and the Sabbath.
TheologicalSignificance: Jesus anchors His argument in a priest's name — Abiathar — and a hungry fugitive eating holy bread. I believe the point is mercy over ritual: if David could eat the shewbread in his need, the Sabbath was never meant to starve God's people, and the Lord of the Sabbath knows it.
